paradox.label: All 205 picks together
paradox.note: Looks like proof that later games are better.

paradox.label: Within one platform
paradox.note: Centre both columns on each system's own mean and it vanishes.

paradox.label: Between platforms
paradox.note: The real effect: long-lived platforms have stronger canons.

systems.name: Atari 2600
systems.note: Created the third-party software industry

picks.note: 255 screens from a procedural seed in 4KB; the pre-NES platformer
Fuel as a timer and a procedurally generated river; Carol Shaw's landmark
The best-selling original 2600 game; the neutral zone is pure design
The first action-adventure and the first Easter egg
Rotor-pack flight, dynamite, and a laser helmet; late-era 2600 mastery

systems.name: Atari 7800
systems.note: MARIA chip; arcade ports but a thin library

picks.note: You golf, then fight ninjas on the walk to your ball. Genuinely great
MARIA's sprite count doing what the 2600 never could; the system's signature
Split-screen 3D future-sport with procedurally generated music
A Zelda-like with Grandpa Munster; the 7800's most ambitious cart
Operation Wolf-style shooting with branching paths

systems.name: ColecoVision
systems.note: Arcade-accurate ports were the entire pitch

picks.note: The pack-in that proved arcade-accurate home ports were possible
Isometric scrolling flight, close enough to the arcade to matter
Rotating gates turn a Pac-Man maze into a shifting puzzle
Digging, apple-crushing, and the best-regarded ColecoVision cart
Launch-window horizontal shooter; showed off the TMS9918 sprites

systems.name: Amstrad CPC
systems.note: Better palette than the Spectrum, worse scrolling

picks.note: The CPC's showcase: 16-colour parallax that the Spectrum could not touch
Isometric puzzle-adventure with timed NPC routines; a CPC high-water mark
The expanded CPC version with extra rooms; flick-screen rescue adventure
A CPC-exclusive Bomberman done better than most licensed versions
Late-era CPC with full-colour sprite animation and real scrolling

systems.name: Capcom CPS-1
systems.note: The Street Fighter II board

picks.note: Playable bosses and mirror matches; the board's defining revision
Set the scrolling-brawler template the whole genre copied
Brutal, gorgeous, and the launch showcase for the hardware
Momentum-based acrobatics and set-pieces far beyond 1989 norms
Four wildly asymmetric characters, each with a mech suit

systems.name: Capcom CPS-2
systems.note: Encrypted "suicide battery" board; peak 2D Capcom

picks.game: Marvel vs. Capcom: Clash of Super Heroes
picks.note: Assists and tag-outs; the crossover-fighter formula locks in here
Three selectable combat systems and 30+ characters
The best-looking brawler ever made and still never ported
Inventory, branching routes, and spell systems inside a brawler
Cave's only Capcom board shooter; the last CPS-2 release

systems.name: Capcom CPS-3
systems.note: Exactly 6 games; highest-resolution 2D sprite work of the era

picks.note: Parries. Twenty-five years of competitive play and still unsolved

picks.game: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Heritage for the Future
picks.note: Stand on/off as a second resource layer; one of the weirdest great fighters
Added Urien and parry-timing refinements; the bridge to 3rd Strike
RPG levelling in an arcade fighter; the launch title, unported until 2022
The risky reboot: all-new roster, hand-animated at absurd frame counts

systems.name: Famicom
systems.note: Same hardware as NES; ~300 titles never left Japan

picks.note: Shigesato Itoi's suburban-America RPG; no English release until 2015

picks.game: Fire Emblem: Ankoku Ryu to Hikari no Tsurugi
picks.note: Permadeath tactics RPG; the series' first 13 years were Japan-only
The direct design ancestor of Resident Evil, down to the mansion
Physics-driven star projectile and an expanded-sound-chip score
A competition prize cart that pushes more sprites than the NES should allow

systems.name: Game Boy
systems.note: 118.69M is GB+GBC combined; split here by common estimate

picks.note: The pack-in that sold the hardware; still the purest game ever bundled
Link-cable trading turned a handheld into a social network

picks.game: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening
picks.note: A Zelda with no Zelda; dense, funny, and built for a 2.6-inch screen
Introduced Wario and a non-linear overworld at 4x the sprite size of SML1
Isolation horror in four shades of green; no map, no mercy

systems.name: Game Boy Advance
systems.note: 32-bit ARM7 handheld; the 2D craft endpoint

picks.note: An original Metroid built for the hardware, with the SA-X turning exploration into a hunt
The soul-collection system; the best-balanced Igavania
A rhythm combo system wrapped around the saddest script Nintendo ever shipped
Perfect-information turn-based war with zero randomness
200 five-second games; invented the microgame as a form

systems.name: Game Boy Color
systems.note: Backwards compatible; 118.69M GB+GBC combined

picks.note: Two full regions, a day/night clock, and breeding on 8-bit hardware

picks.game: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons / Ages
picks.note: Two games that link into one via password; Capcom out-Zelda-ing Nintendo
A full top-down MGS with codec drama and VR missions, built in 8-bit
An invincible protagonist turns a platformer into a lock-and-key puzzle box
Released after the GBA launched; the most technically absurd GBC game ever

systems.name: Game Gear
systems.note: Backlit colour handheld; 6 hours on 6 AAs

picks.game: Shining Force: The Sword of Hajya
picks.note: A full console-scale SRPG campaign on a handheld in 1993
The 8-bit Sonic line's best level design, not a port of anything
Arabian-nights RPG with a genie companion; criminally unknown
Swap between five ninja with distinct kits to open the hub

picks.game: Land of Illusion starring Mickey Mouse
picks.note: Castle of Illusion's sequel line; bigger, with light RPG progression

systems.name: Game & Watch
systems.note: One game per unit; invented the D-pad

picks.note: The dual-screen clamshell and the first cross-shaped D-pad
Unit one. Juggling. The entire handheld industry starts here
Timing-based rescue loop; the purest score-chase in the line
Two-screen conveyor coordination with both hands doing different jobs
A full dungeon crawl with items and bosses rendered in fixed LCD segments

systems.name: Intellivision
systems.note: 16-bit CPU in 1979; disc controller and overlays

picks.note: The first god game / city-builder, two-player and resource-driven
First-person grid-based dungeon crawling on a console in 1983
The pack-in; scoring curve engineered for the million-point chase
The disc controller's best use case; still a sharp twin-input game
The best home version of the arcade game by a long way

systems.name: Atari Lynx
systems.note: First colour backlit handheld; hardware sprite scaling

picks.note: The launch pack-in; the Lynx's hardware scaling finally justified
149 tile-logic levels; originated here before becoming a Windows staple
Six game modes and co-op over a comm-link cable
Afterburner-style scaling that no other handheld of the era could do
Filled-polygon 3D on a 1989 handheld, released in 1995

systems.name: MAME 2003-Plus
systems.note: Curated set of the golden-age coin-op canon

picks.note: Non-violent, pattern-based, and the first game with a mass audience
Cutscenes, a story, and jumping; Miyamoto's first design
Capture-and-dual-fighter risk/reward on top of Galaxian
Invented twin-stick controls; still one of the hardest games ever shipped
Co-op bubble physics and a true ending that requires two players

systems.name: Mega Drive / Genesis
systems.note: 68000 + YM2612 FM; Sega's only real win vs Nintendo

picks.note: Spin dash plus split-screen versus; Sega's commercial and design peak
Weapon-combination system and sprite scaling nobody else attempted
Yuzo Koshiro's FM house soundtrack and the genre's best-weighted hits
Manga-panel cutscenes and combo macros; closes a four-game arc
Grab-and-throw traversal; released into the Saturn's shadow and forgotten

systems.name: MSX
systems.note: A standard, not a machine; Konami's lab

picks.note: Kojima's debut and the origin of avoid-don't-fight as a design rule
Two swappable heroes over a huge interconnected castle; years ahead
The MSX2 Castlevania: key-hunting and room exploration instead of linear stages
Kojima's first production credit; multiple endings in 1986
The Adventures of Lolo puzzle lineage starts here

systems.name: MSX2
systems.note: V9938 VDP; where Kojima learned to direct

picks.note: Crouching, radar, and a script that embarrasses most 32-bit games
Snatcher rebuilt as a body-part-targeting RPG
The MSX2's technical ceiling: smooth scroll, huge bosses, SCC audio
Branching routes and a time-travel plot inside a Gradius spin-off
Compile's vertical shooter line at its most polished

systems.name: Nintendo 64
systems.note: Smallest library of its gen; analog stick + 4 controller ports

picks.game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
picks.note: Z-targeting solved 3D combat for everyone who came after
Invented the analog 3D moveset and the free camera in one go
Objective-based stealth shooting plus the console split-screen deathmatch

picks.game: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
picks.note: A three-day clock and a doomed town; the strangest first-party Nintendo game
The collect-a-thon at its most tightly designed, before the genre bloated

systems.name: Neo Geo
systems.note: Identical arcade and home hardware; 14-year lifespan

picks.note: Branching paths and animation density nobody has matched since
The T.O.P. system and just-defend; SNK's mechanical high point
No story, just the roster; the series' balance benchmark
Speed/power stance split over the prettiest sprite work SNK ever drew
Weapon clashes and one-hit-kill tension; deflection as a core system

systems.name: NES
systems.note: Western branding of the Famicom (US 1985); 61.91M is the combined NES/Famicom figure

picks.note: The 8-bit platformer's final form: world map, suits, scrolling that never stutters
Battery-backed saves invented the long-form console game
Non-linear stage select plus the best NES soundtrack ever authored
Branching paths and swappable partners; the VRC6 chip adds three audio channels
Shipped in 1993 on hardware from 1983 and still looks impossible

systems.name: Neo Geo Pocket
systems.note: Mono model; microswitched clicky stick

picks.note: A real KOF on a mono handheld, built around the clicky microswitch stick
Weapon fighting with chibi sprites; the mono library's other standout
Launch title; deep enough that people still rank it over the colour sports games
Connect-the-pairs under time pressure; a perfect one-AA-battery game
Arcadey football with the arcade series' feel intact

systems.name: Neo Geo Pocket Color
systems.note: Best fighting-game handheld ever built

picks.game: SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millennium
picks.note: The best handheld fighting game ever made, by a wide margin
SNK building a Sonic game, and getting the physics genuinely right

picks.game: SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters' Clash
picks.note: A deckbuilder with two rival carts; the system's cult classic
Programmed action queues; a mech SRPG from the Shadow Hearts team
Branching mission structure built for short handheld sessions

systems.name: Odyssey 2 / Videopac
systems.note: Built-in keyboard; board-game/videogame hybrids

picks.note: Editable mazes and smart ghosts; Atari sued it off the shelves and won
Ladder-and-boulder timing with a key-collection loop
Control a swarm, not a character; uses the console's weird plane-blending
A board game plus a video game; the Master Strategy Series' best idea
The system's technical showpiece and its hardest game

systems.name: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16
systems.note: 8-bit CPU, 16-bit video; #1 in Japan in 1988

picks.note: Gradius-grade weapon layering; the shooter that defined the hardware
A pinball table with bosses, HP bars, and a death-metal score
Headbutt physics and meat-powered rage modes; NEC's mascot attempt
The Star Soldier line's cleanest entry, with 2- and 5-minute score modes
Hex-grid lunar warfare; still one of the best console wargames

systems.name: PC Engine CD
systems.note: First CD-ROM games console add-on anywhere

picks.note: Branching stages, a second playable character, and Redbook audio
Voice acting and a CD score in 1989; the first great CD-ROM game
Elemental armour loadouts over a full hard-rock CD soundtrack
The pack-in for the Duo and still a reference-grade horizontal shooter
Arcade CD technical showpiece; sprite counts the hardware should refuse

systems.name: Pokemon Mini
systems.note: Smallest cartridge console ever made; exactly 10 games

picks.note: Three solid puzzle modes; the most game on the smallest cartridge console
Uses the built-in rumble and tilt sensor as core mechanics
Tetris with a catching meta-layer on a 96x64 screen
Five minigames; Japan-only and the system's most charming cart
Five card rulesets including a full Uno clone with AI personalities

systems.name: Ports
systems.note: Not emulation: native rebuilds of released engines from source

picks.note: The source release made it the most ported game in history; runs anywhere
True polygonal 3D plus the modding culture that produced modern FPS design
One person, five years, freeware; the indie era's founding document
An open reimplementation; the original 3D-platformer-with-guns
Shareware vertical shooter with a deep upgrade economy, now GPL

systems.name: PlayStation
systems.note: First console past 100M; killed the cartridge

picks.note: Cinematic direction, fourth-wall breaks, and stealth as a full genre
Pre-rendered backgrounds and a 3-disc script; made RPGs mainstream in the West
Named half a genre; the inverted castle is still a structural flex
Two interlocking scenarios; fixed cameras used as deliberate dread
Licence tests and 140 cars; the simulation racer arrives on console

systems.name: PlayStation Portable
systems.note: Console-class 3D in a handheld

picks.note: Base management plus co-op; a mainline MGS built for a handheld
Ad-hoc multiplayer made this the biggest handheld game in Japan
Four drum inputs command an army; nothing else plays like it

picks.game: God of War: Chains of Olympus
picks.note: Proved a handheld could carry a full-scale action-adventure
You tilt the world, not the character; two shoulder buttons, total control

systems.name: Sega CD
systems.note: CD audio + scaling/rotation ASIC; FMV era epicentre

picks.note: Time travel changes the level geometry; two full soundtracks
Kojima's cyberpunk visual novel; the only English console release it ever got
Animated cutscenes and a sung theme; the CD RPG that justified the add-on
Falcom action-RPG with a fully voiced comedy script
The arcade-complete Final Fight nobody else managed, with CD audio

systems.name: Super Famicom
systems.note: JP library is ~2x the US RPG count

picks.note: Six protagonists, class-change trees, three-player co-op; fan-translated for decades
Generational inheritance mechanics on enormous single-map chapters
Square's dragon-raising SRPG; never officially localised
The "mantra" system lets you type spell words the engine parses
An elastic fishing-line grapple with real spring physics in 1994

systems.name: SG-1000
systems.note: Launched the same day as the Famicom and lost instantly

picks.note: Yuji Naka's first game; flower-collecting with a bear chasing you
Herd the birds home; Sega's first real original character design
100 rooms of key-and-door logic; the best-regarded SG-1000 game
Vertically scrolling shuriken stealth; later an arcade hit
Compile's early shooter, and the best-looking thing on the hardware

systems.name: SuperGrafx
systems.note: 5 dedicated games + 2 hybrids. That is the whole library

picks.note: The single reason to own the hardware; near-arcade parallax
Built from scratch for the dual-VDC; the only original SuperGrafx shooter of note
The last SuperGrafx exclusive ever released
Anime tie-in platformer; mostly a curiosity
The launch title, alone on the system for four months, and not good

systems.name: Master System
systems.note: Dominant in Brazil and PAL Europe, not the US

picks.note: First-person animated 3D dungeons and a female lead, in 1987

picks.game: Wonder Boy III: The Dragon's Trap
picks.note: Animal transformations as a metroidvania key system
An unapologetic Zelda clone that is genuinely as good as Zelda
Built into the console in some regions; janky, inventive, janken bosses
A completely different game from the 16-bit one, with its own level design

systems.name: Super Nintendo
systems.note: US launch 1991; Mode 7 + S-SMP audio defined the 16-bit look and sound

picks.note: Environmental storytelling with zero cutscenes; the genre's reference text
Multiple endings, no random encounters, Toriyama + Mitsuda + the Dream Team

picks.game: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
picks.note: Two overlaid worlds; the template every top-down Zelda still follows
Cape physics, Yoshi, and a secret-exit map that rewards obsession
Pre-rendered SGI sprites made a 16-bit machine look next-gen

systems.name: Virtual Boy
systems.note: Commercial failure; 22 games total, 14 in the West

picks.note: Uses the parallax layers as actual level geometry you move between
The first Megami Tensei game released in the West, on the worst possible console
First-person boxing where the stereoscopy genuinely helps you read punches
Depth makes the table read correctly; the system's best-feeling game
Wireframe 3D combat; unreadable and fascinating in equal measure

systems.name: WonderSwan
systems.note: Gunpei Yokoi's last design; 40 hours on one AA

picks.note: Gunpei Yokoi's namesake puzzler; slide line segments into unbroken paths
A real Klonoa game with the grab-and-throw loop intact in mono
Ghosts 'n Goblins rebuilt, not downported, for a 1-bit screen
A rhythm-platformer hybrid years before the genre existed
Mono horror vignettes using the vertical screen orientation

systems.name: WonderSwan Color
systems.note: Square's handheld home before the GBA deal

picks.note: Square's remake line lived on WSC first; new art, rebalanced
Trigger-point exploration and item-durability combat; later ported widely
Won a WonderWitch dev contest and got a real release; a bullet-hell cult legend
Chibi Guilty Gear with the roman-cancel feel surprisingly intact
The free-scenario SaGa structure, playable on a AA battery

systems.name: ZX Spectrum
systems.note: Colour clash and the UK bedroom-coder industry

picks.note: 20 single-screen rooms, in-game music on a beeper; the UK canon's origin
Filmation isometric engine; invented a visual language overnight
Two characters with different abilities who combine into one unit
An open galaxy in 48KB; procedural generation as a survival tactic
A 60-room mansion and the most famous bug in British gaming
